claim: The official MCP registry is the closest MCP-native analogue to a tool registry: server.json declares a name and an immutable, unique-per-publish version string -- 'The version string MUST be unique for each publication of the server. Once published, the version string (and other metadata) cannot be changed.' The registry recommends semver but accepts other formats, explicitly prohibits version-range strings (the page's own table marks ^1.2.3, ~1.2.3, >=1.2.3, <=1.2.3 and >1.2.3 as 'Prohibited'), and computes a 'latest' pointer via stated comparison rules: 'When a server is published, the MCP Registry will attempt to parse its version as a semantic version string for sorting purposes, and will mark the version as “latest” if appropriate. If parsing fails, the version will always be marked as “latest”.' Corrected 2026-09-09: the previous snippet wrapped 'MUST' in fabricated markdown-bold asterisks not present in the rendered page; the previous read field used straight quotes where the page uses curly quotes. This is version pinning plus a moving 'latest' alias, not the alias-to-immutable-version indirection seen in prompt/model registries.

Per that text, this May-2026 paper (Future Internet journal, within the recency window) proposes a three-layer trust framework for the official MCP registry -- RFC 8615 Well-Known URIs for domain-bound server identity, Sigstore Keyless signing (Fulcio/Rekor-style, no long-lived keys) to bind published server artifacts to audited CI/CD, and JCS(RFC 8785)+JWS for live capability-update integrity -- and is explicit about what registry acceptance does NOT prove: "Acceptance proves that the descriptor and ownership checks passed -- not that downstream directories have synchronized or that the server is safe."

claim: Sigstore (built for container/software signing) extends to model artifacts: hash the model plus its files/metadata into a serialized manifest, sign the manifest keylessly (Fulcio issues a short-lived cert bound to a CI/CD or human identity), and record the signing event in the public Rekor transparency log; a consumer verifies by matching the cert identity and confirming Rekor inclusion, not by trusting a long-lived key. Dated April 2025 -- older than the 2026-03+ recency preference, flagged accordingly, but it is the concrete signing mechanism this pass found for model artifacts specifically (vs. container images).
query: model artifact signing Sigstore transparency log ML model provenance 2026
read: using Sigstore's transparency log component, Rekor, to record signing events, enabling anyone to verify the model's signature against the log.
snippet: a cryptographic hash of the model and all its files and metadata is generated and written to a serialized manifest.
title: Model authenticity and transparency with Sigstore - Red Hat Emerging Technologies
topic: Signing an ML model artifact itself with Sigstore (manifest hash, Fulcio identity cert, Rekor transparency log)

claim: MLflow's Model Registry is the same two-layer shape as the prompt registries above: registered model versions are immutable and strictly sequential (a new registration always increments the version number), while aliases (e.g. champion/challenger, replacing the deprecated Staging/Production stage labels) are mutable named pointers. Resolving an alias via the URI models:/<name>@<alias> returns the specific immutable version it currently points to; promotion is a governed, auditable, single-call reassignment of the alias, with the prior version always still addressable for rollback.
query: model registry aliases stages immutable versions MLflow Vertex AI SageMaker 2026
read: you can create an alias named champion that points to version 1 of a model named MyModel. You can then refer to version 1 of MyModel by using the URI models:/MyModel@champion.
snippet: Model aliases allow you to assign a mutable, named reference to a particular version of a registered model.
title: ML Model Registry | MLflow AI Platform
topic: Model registry structure: immutable sequential versions plus mutable named aliases, and what resolving an alias returns (MLflow)

claim: The OCI reference model (registry/repository/tag-or-digest) is a general-purpose, already-standardized version of the same alias-vs-immutable-version split seen in the prompt and model registries above: a human-friendly mutable tag ("latest", "v1.0") always resolves to an immutable content digest (SHA256), so naming "the current X" by tag never stops every consumer from getting a verifiable, pinned artifact underneath. Existing repo research (X-cap-capability-registry-004, -005, -008) already established OCI artifacts / ORAS as a distribution mechanism for agent skills and capability records with signing support -- this record adds the specific tag-vs-digest resolution mechanics a Models/Prompts/Tools/Datasets registry card would need to cite if it reused OCI as its artifact-reference shape.
query: OCI artifact reference specification package registry standard version resolution 2026
read: Reference by a digest is a unique, immutable identifier for a specific image or artifact
snippet: Tags are mutable. This means that the same tag can point to different digests over time.
title: Reference | OCI Registry As Storage
topic: OCI artifact reference shape (registry/repo/tag-or-digest) as a candidate open standard for a shared registry record

claim: SLSA provenance is a signed statement whose subject is an artifact digest and whose predicate binds that digest to a build definition and a builder identity (builder.id, "URI indicating the transitive closure of the trusted build platform") plus run details. It is built for software build outputs (source repo + build platform as the primary inputs) and has no built-in vocabulary for prompts, models, or datasets -- fitting it to those artifact types would mean defining custom buildTypes rather than using the standard as-is. Answers the open-standard question directly: SLSA/in-toto attestations are a plausible provenance layer to wrap AROUND a registry record (who/what produced this artifact), but not, by themselves, the registry record's resolution mechanism (name+version-constraint -> specific artifact) -- that role is closer to what OCI references (record 007) or the MCP registry's server.json (record 003) already provide.
query: in-toto SLSA provenance attestation artifact registry record standard non-software artifacts
read: URI indicating the transitive closure of the trusted build platform
snippet: verifiable information about software artifacts describing where, when, and how something was produced
title: SLSA Provenance v1.1
topic: SLSA provenance as a candidate open standard for a registry record: what it binds, and its fit (or lack of it) for prompts/models/datasets
